minutes.headline: Select Board approved two utility licenses and held three police bylaw articles for town counsel, amid a water district dispute.
minutes.summary: The board approved license agreements with Unitil and Boston Gas for the middle/high school project, signed the town meeting warrants, and heard a heated exchange with a water commissioner over a proposed water extension to Lancaster. The police chief presented four warrant articles (Willard Lake vehicles, public marijuana smoking, pawn brokers, sex offender residency); the lake article was recommended, the others deferred pending town counsel review. The board then went into executive session on the DPW union contract.

public_comment.topic: A water commissioner objected to not being told the board would discuss the Lancaster water extension, and defended the district's process and the no-cost condition.
A Lions Club representative promoted Saturday's fundraising event at Andrews Hall and thanked a volunteer.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved license agreements with Unitil and Boston Gas for the middle/high school project.
The board recommended the Willard Lake vehicle bylaw article for town meeting.
The board deferred its recommendation on the public marijuana smoking bylaw to town meeting, pending town counsel input.
The pawn broker bylaw will be reworked with town counsel and may move to a later town meeting; the sex offender residency bylaw was deferred for legal review.
A water commissioner objected to the board discussing a water extension to Lancaster without notice; a public agenda item with the water commissioners is tentatively set for May.

why_it_matters: Town meeting voters will see the lake vehicle article with a board recommendation, but the marijuana, pawn broker and sex offender residency bylaws may come without one or be pushed to a later meeting.
The Lancaster water extension is conditioned on costing the Lunenburg water district nothing, so water customers will want to see how that condition is documented before any commitment.
Article 13 would move first-year AFSCME contract funding from the salary reserve into departments, which affects how the town budget, mostly taxes, is allocated.
watch_next: Public agenda item with the water commissioners, tentatively May 12 or 19.
Whether the board meets April 28 before town meeting, to be decided next week.
